title: Cannot recognize html img tag style if add img tag dynamically
summary: The reporter adds an tag dynamically via JavaScript (createElement) with a base64 data URI, and the image does not render with its style as expected in the generated PDF. The output differs from what browsers produce.
key_detail: wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6 on Windows 11; img added via window.onload with data:image/png;base64 source
evidence: Image added at runtime via document.createElement/window.onload requires a JS engine; matrix §5 strips <script>/DOM APIs at load, --enable-javascript ignored.
author: CY-Qiu

title: wkhtmltopdf doesn't recognize justify-content
summary: CSS flexbox property justify-content: space-evenly works in the HTML/browser but is not honored when rendering a PDF. The user reports the layout difference while generating a PDF.
key_detail: justify-content : space-evenly not supported in the Qt WebKit rendering
evidence: Matrix §2.7: justify-content (incl. space-evenly) marked Implemented in internal/layout/flex.go with TestFlexSpaceEvenly.
author: KsentiniHaitham

title: HTML page turns completely white/empty
summary: Converting a live Angular-rendered invoice page to PDF succeeds without errors but produces a completely blank PDF. The reporter suspects the page's JavaScript/Angular rendering is the cause.
key_detail: wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6 (with patched qt), Linux Mint 19.1 and Docker; full command output shows no error despite blank result
evidence: Angular-SPA content is JS-generated; gowkhtmltopdf strips JavaScript at load (matrix §5) — framework pages unsupported.
author: mateusfmello

title: ContentNotFoundError is thrown if HTML file contains links to filenames with multiple dots '.'
summary: Converting HTML that links or scripts files whose filenames contain multiple dots (e.g. materialdesignicons.min.css) fails with a ContentNotFoundError. Removing the extra dot in the filename makes it work.
workaround: Removing the extra '.' (e.g. using materialdesignicons.css instead of .min.css) avoids the error
evidence: Loader has no dot-count restriction: FetchSub/resolveReference resolve refs via net/url and os paths (internal/load/load.go).
author: ghost

title: PDF with hundreds of images, how to avoid loading all images concurrently
summary: A PDF containing hundreds of HTTPS images loads them all concurrently, flooding the web server with requests. The reporter asks whether images can be batch-loaded or concurrency limited.
key_detail: Hundreds of images loaded over HTTPS all at once
evidence: No concurrent image fan-out: image fetcher pulls each img on demand, single-threaded, size-capped cache (internal/imageout).
author: nicodemuz

title: Vanilla Javascript won't render
summary: A simple HTML file with a canvas-based pie chart drawn by vanilla JavaScript renders fine in the browser but produces no chart in the PDF. The reporter stripped all CSS to isolate the problem and asks how to debug it.
key_detail: macOS 11.6, wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6 (with patched qt); uses canvas getContext("2d") to draw the pie chart
evidence: Canvas pie chart drawn by vanilla JS; matrix §5 strips JavaScript at load — JS-driven rendering out of scope.

title: Q: why does the font look so bad?

title: Generating PDFs with many images fails.
summary: Generating large PDFs with many images fails with 'Warning: Failed to load file:///... (ignore)' once the OS open-file limit is exceeded, silently dropping images from the output. The reporter suggests the implementation need not hold all files open in parallel.
